title: Per-scope credential workflow, naming standards, rotation automation, and audit playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current API token surface mixes user long-lived tokens, ad-hoc service keys, and admin scopes in ways that make least-privilege enforcement, rotation, and auditability hard. This leads to: stale keys lingering, insufficient per-scope visibility, difficulty mapping keys into RBAC v2 role grants, and manual rotations that cause outages.

Goal: Deliver a unified, operationally simple credential model that: (1) enforces per-scope keys tied to RBAC v2 grants, (2) provides automated rotation and expiry policies for different token classes, (3) standardizes naming and provenance for auditability, (4) offers migration tools for legacy tokens, and (5) integrates with SSO/SAML session lifetimes for user token exchange.

Constraints and requirements:
- Backwards compatibility for existing long-lived keys during migration window (6-12 weeks).
- Minimal runtime overhead on inference control plane token validation (validator service must remain <2ms p50).
- Audit logs must contain token_id, issuer, policy_snapshot, action, route, and effective_role for every auth event.
- Support both human (SSO-backed) tokens and machine/service tokens with distinct policies.
- Admin UX: allow emergency revoke, per-owner token listing, and token metadata for owner/contact.

Proposed design summary:
1) Token classes:
   - Ephemeral user tokens: exchanged from SAML/OIDC session via assertion exchange. TTL default 1h, bound to session_id and device_id. Intended for interactive console/API calls.
   - Scoped service tokens: created via Control Plane API, scoped to specific RBAC v2 role grants (e.g., model:read, infer:write). TTL default 90 days with recommended automatic rotation at 45d.
   - Short-lived service credentials (workloads): issued to infra (k8s, batch jobs) via workload-identity flow, TTL 24h, auto-rotated by infra-side agents.
   - Admin bearer tokens: restricted to org-admin scope, short TTL (8h) and require 2-step rotation (rotation + approval) for new issuance.

2) Naming and provenance standard (string metadata embedded in token metadata and ledger):
   - service/<env>/<team>/<purpose>/<ownerHandle>/<YYYYMMDD>
   - user/<username>/<device>/<SSO-provider>/<YYYYMMDD>
   - transient/<workflow>/<jobid>/<YYYYMMDD>
   This establishes deterministic token_id prefixes and improves search in audit logs.

3) Token ledger and metadata store:
   - Central ledger (immutable append-only table) stores token_id, hashed_secret, creator, owner, scopes, role_snapshot, issue_ts, expiry_ts, rotation_history_ids, status (active/revoked/rotated), and human-friendly name. Ledger entries are write-once; rotations append a new record and link to previous via rotation_history_ids.

4) Rotation automation and policy engine:
   - Rotation worker runs in control plane, driven by policy rules: TTL, idle-time-to-rotate, and pin-to-owner rules. Policy decisions produce planned-rotation events; owners are notified via email/console and auto-rotate occurs after grace period unless owner postpones. Emergency rotate and immediate revoke endpoints exist for SRE/SEC ops.

5) RBAC v2 mapping:
   - Each token ledger entry stores role_snapshot: immutable snapshot of RBAC grants at issuance. Token validator computes effective_role by combining role_snapshot and dynamic overrides (e.g., temporary deny). This preserves reproducible access evaluation for audit and for rollback during incidents.

6) Audit logging and observability:
   - Auth events must emit structured logs containing: token_id, token_name, issuer, effective_role, route, request_id, client_ip, user_agent, timestamp, and token_origin (sso|service|transient).
   - Logs forwarded to central ELK/Databricks + long-term S3 archive for 13 months. Alerting rules detect: token replay anomalies, sudden spike in token creation, token use from unexpected geo, and failed validations.

7) SSO/SAML integration:
   - Implement SAML assertion exchange to mint ephemeral user tokens with mapped RBAC v2 claims. Map SAML group attributes to RBAC roles during exchange. Honor SAML session lifetime as a max cap for TTL. Provide tooling for IdP admins to verify session lifetimes and token issuance logs.

8) Migration plan:
   - Phase 0 (week 0-2): Read-only ledger ingestion of existing tokens and classification into token classes.
   - Phase 1 (week 3-6): Soft-enforce new validator: accept legacy tokens but annotate logs with "legacy=true" and surface owners to console for rotation nudges.
   - Phase 2 (week 7-10): Auto-rotate eligible legacy tokens into scoped service tokens (with owner approval window).
   - Phase 3 (week 11-12): Enforce denylist for stale legacy tokens and require re-issuance.

9) Rollout and canary strategy:
   - Canary subset: 5% of traffic routed to new validator and ledger-backed policy engine with mirroring of auth decisions from old system; compare diffs nightly and block on >0.1% decision mismatch.
   - Gradual ramp to 100% after 4 successful canary cycles.

10) Metrics and success criteria:
   - % tokens with per-scope metadata > 95% within 10 weeks.
   - Mean time to rotate (automated) < 48h for scheduled rotations.
   - Auth validator overhead p50 < 2ms.
   - Number of active legacy tokens < 5% after migration window.

11) Runbook snippets (revocation/incident):
   - If compromise detected: identify token_id, call /v1/admin/revoke/{token_id}, rotate dependent service keys via control plane automation, and run retrospective to identify blast radius using ledger role_snapshot.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Security/Per-scope+Credential+Workflow+Design
- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1482
- Token ledger schema: https://docs.redwood.ai/control-plane/token-ledger-schema.md

Open decisions (needs design/security sign-off):
- Default TTL for scoped service tokens (90d proposed) vs shorter by default (60d) to reduce exposure.
- Whether to require 2FA for creating admin bearer tokens in console.
- Retention window for audit logs (13 months proposed) vs legal constraints for EU customers.

Next steps:
- Finalize TTL defaults with Security (due 2026-03-18).
- Implement validator shim and ledger ingestion (ENG-27390, assigned).
- Start Canary rollout plan and alerting (ENG-27500).
